parameters.jsCode:
const tf = $('Webhook').first()?.json?.body?.target_framework || 'net8.0';

let knownPatterns = `THESE FACTS ARE ALREADY VERIFIED. DO NOT SPEND TOOL CALLS RE-RESEARCHING THEM.
TARGET_FRAMEWORK: ${tf}
OLD_FRAMEWORKS: net6.0, net7.0, netcoreapp3.1

PACKAGE_MAPPINGS:
- Microsoft.AspNetCore.* -> remove (built into SDK)
- Microsoft.Extensions.* -> remove or update to matching version (built-in)
- Newtonsoft.Json -> keep, update to latest; or migrate to System.Text.Json
- EntityFrameworkCore -> update to matching version; watch for breaking changes
- Swashbuckle.AspNetCore -> update for compatibility
- NUnit/xUnit/MSTest -> update to latest; no API breaks expected
- AutoMapper -> update to latest
- Moq -> update to 4.20+; remove SponsorLink if present
- Pomelo.EntityFrameworkCore.MySql -> update to matching version

CSPROJ_CHANGES:
- <TargetFramework>... -> <TargetFramework>${tf}</TargetFramework>
- <Nullable>enable</Nullable> -> add if missing
- <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings> -> add if missing

BREAKING_CHANGES:
- IHostingEnvironment -> IWebHostEnvironment
- HttpContext.GetTokenAsync -> requires Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication namespace
- JsonSerializer default casing changed -> set JsonSerializerOptions.PropertyNamingPolicy explicitly
- EF Core: Owned entity table splitting behaviour changed
- DateOnly/TimeOnly types now fully supported

SKIP_DB_TESTS_REASON: No live DB connection string available in migration CI environment. Tests filtered by Category!=DatabaseTest and Category!=IntegrationTest.

COMMON_BUILD_ERRORS:
- CS0246: missing using or package ref -> check package mappings above
- CS8600/CS8603: nullable warnings -> add ? annotations or null checks
- NETSDK1045: SDK version too low -> upgrade dotnet SDK on host
- NU1202: package not compatible -> update to compatible version`;

return [{ json: { known_patterns: knownPatterns } }];

parameters.command:
=BASE=/projects/migration-{{ $('Webhook').first().json.body.job_id }}

echo '=== REPOSITORY FILE TREE ==='
cd $BASE && git ls-files | grep -Ev '^(.*/)?(wwwroot|node_modules|bin|obj|\.vs|packages)/' | grep -Ev '\.(min\.js|min\.css|map|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|svg|ico|woff2?|ttf|eot)$'
echo ''

export DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1
export DOTNET_NOLOGO=1

TFM={{ $('Webhook').first().json.body.target_framework || 'net8.0' }}

# The Upgrade Assistant analyses COMPILED ASSEMBLIES, so a freshly cloned repo
# gives it nothing to look at. Build first; tolerate failure and show the tail
# so the agent can see why if it did not build.
echo '=== BUILD (required before analysis) ==='
cd "$BASE" && timeout 300 dotnet build -v quiet -nologo 2>&1 | tail -15 || true
echo ''

# Point it at the solution (or a project). Measured on the fixture: analysing the
# .sln found 47 incidents across both projects, while "--source Folder" on the
# repo root found 0.
UA_TARGET=$(find "$BASE" -name '*.sln' | head -1)
[ -z "$UA_TARGET" ] && UA_TARGET=$(find "$BASE" -name '*.csproj' | head -1)
# --report resolves relative to the directory of the analysed path, so a relative
# name lands predictably at $BASE/ua-report.json. Absolute paths get concatenated.
rm -f "$BASE/ua-report.json"
# Discard stdout/stderr: on a non-English locale the tool crashes AFTER writing
# the report ("Could not find color or style 'surligner'"), so trust the file.
[ -n "$UA_TARGET" ] && timeout 240 upgrade-assistant analyze "$UA_TARGET" --targetFramework "$TFM" --report ua-report --serializer JSON --non-interactive >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# Emitted HERE, before the file dumps, on purpose: the formatter truncates this
# stdout at 12000 chars and truncation eats the tail. These findings are the
# highest-signal part of the output, so they must not be what gets cut.
echo '=== UPGRADE ASSISTANT FINDINGS ==='
node /projects/migration_backend/scripts/distill_ua_report.js "$BASE/ua-report.json" 2>/dev/null || echo 'NO_UPGRADE_ASSISTANT_REPORT'
# Remove it from the working tree so Part 2 cannot commit the report into the PR.
rm -f "$BASE/ua-report.json"
echo ''

echo '=== CSPROJ FILES ==='
find $BASE -name '*.csproj' | head -20 | xargs -I {} sh -c 'echo "--- {} ---"; cat "{}"'

echo '=== SOLUTION FILES ==='
find $BASE -name '*.sln' | head -5

echo '=== PROGRAM/STARTUP ==='
find $BASE \( -name 'Program.cs' -o -name 'Startup.cs' \) | head -10 | xargs -I {} sh -c 'echo "--- {} ---"; cat "{}"'

echo '=== CONTROLLERS (first 3) ==='
find $BASE -path '*/Controllers/*.cs' | head -3 | xargs -I {} sh -c 'echo "--- {} ---"; head -80 "{}"'

echo '=== END OF CONTEXT ==='

parameters.text:
={{
'You are a formatter. Convert the RESEARCH BRIEF below into a migration plan that matches the JSON schema exactly.
' +
'You do NOT do your own analysis. Do not add findings that are not in the brief. Do not drop findings that are.

' +
'=== THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: EVERY CHANGE MUST STILL COMPILE ===
' +
'A change that compiles is worth more than a change that is elegant. Before you emit ANY old/new pair, run this check:
' +
'  STEP 1. Look at the lines that come immediately AFTER your old snippet in the source.
' +
'  STEP 2. Ask: does any of those lines use a variable your new snippet renamed, removed, or changed the type of?
' +
'           Does any of them call a member that exists on the OLD type but not on the NEW type?
' +
'  STEP 3. If yes to either, your old/new pair is TOO SMALL. Grow it downward to include those lines and rewrite
' +
'           them too. Repeat from STEP 1 until the answer is no.
' +
'  STEP 4. Also check upward: does your new snippet leave a variable declared above it now unused or dangling?
' +
'           If so, include that declaration in the pair and remove it.
' +
'Worked example of the trap: replacing a reader type whose ValidationType property is set on the NEXT line.
' +
'Replacing only the constructor line leaves the property assignment pointing at a type that has no such property
' +
'- that is a compile error. The pair must cover the constructor AND the property line together.
' +
'A type with a similar name or purpose is NEVER guaranteed to expose the same members. Verify the member surface
' +
'of the replacement before assuming a rename is a drop-in.
' +
'If you genuinely cannot see the surrounding lines and cannot determine the call sites, put the file in risk_notes.
' +
'That is the correct outcome - never emit a change you cannot verify compiles.
' +
'BUT: any file reproduced under "=== VERBATIM SOURCE ===" in the brief IS fully visible to you. Never send such a
' +
'file to risk_notes for lack of context - read its lines there and emit the real change.

' +
'=== NEVER SUBSTITUTE A PLACEHOLDER FOR A FIX ===
' +
'A comment such as // TODO, // replaced with X, or an empty body is NOT a migration change. It compiles but
' +
'silently changes behaviour, which is worse than leaving the code alone. Either emit the real replacement, or
' +
'record the item in risk_notes and emit no file_change for it. Never the middle ground.

' +
'RULES:
' +
'- Use the EXACT relative file paths that appear in the brief and the repository file tree. Never invent a path.
' +
'- Never output Microsoft.NETCore.App or Microsoft.AspNetCore.App as packages.
' +
'- Use the resolved_version from the brief for every package. If the brief has no version, set to_version to "" and leave it to the NuGet resolver.
' +
'- Combine all changes to one file into a SINGLE file_changes entry for that file.
' +
'- FORMATTING: old/new values are plain code strings in JSON - never include triple-backtick markdown fences (```) inside them. If the brief contains fenced code blocks, strip the fences and keep only the code.
' +
'- PACKAGE CONSISTENCY: nuget_versions_needed must list EXACTLY the packages marked action "add" or "update" in package_updates - no more, no fewer. A package marked action "remove" must NEVER appear in nuget_versions_needed; it is being deleted, so there is nothing to resolve.
' +
'- ORPHANED IMPORTS: when a package is marked action "remove", or a type is replaced by one from a different namespace, you MUST also emit file_changes entries deleting or rewriting the now-invalid using directives in every file that references that namespace (CS0246). If the brief does not name those files, record it in risk_notes.
' +
'- STALE COMMENTS: if your new code makes a comment or doc-comment inside the snippet false - it names a type,
' +
'  method, overload or version you just replaced - rewrite that comment in the same old/new pair. A comment that
' +
'  describes the code you removed is a defect, not a neutral leftover. Do not enlarge a snippet solely to reach a
' +
'  distant comment; only fix comments already inside the span you are replacing.
' +
'- PRIORITY: anything the brief labels BREAKING is "must". Anything labelled NON-BREAKING is "should". All target_framework_updates are "must". An API that throws at runtime on the target framework is BREAKING and therefore "must", even if it compiles. If unsure, use "must".
' +
'- Anything in the brief under "Unverified / needs human review" goes into risk_notes, NOT into file_changes.
' +
'- RISK NOTES ARE FOR HUMAN DECISIONS, NOT FOR THINGS A COMPILER SETTLES. Never record an item whose only
' +
'  uncertainty is that you could not build, run or test the code - the execution phase builds it and has an
' +
'  error-fixing loop. "Confirm this overload exists", "verify the signature", "a build was not run here" are
' +
'  not risk notes. Record only what a compiler CANNOT answer: data or wire formats crossing a system boundary,
' +
'  callers outside this repository, licensing, and product decisions.
' +
'- estimated_changes MUST be an integer. risk_level MUST be low, medium or high. action MUST be update, remove, add or no_update.
' +
'- Output valid JSON only. Every required property in the schema must be present.

' +
'DETERMINISTIC REPOSITORY PROFILE (source of truth for source_framework):
' +
($('Webhook').first().json.body.repository_profile || '[]') + '

' +
'RESEARCH BRIEF:
' +
($json.research_brief || '') + '

' +
'REPOSITORY FILE TREE AND SOURCE CONTEXT (valid paths only - use this to check the lines around each change):
' +
($('Run Roslyn Upgrade Assistant').first().json.stdout || '').substring(0,12000)
}}

options.systemMessage:
You are a .NET migration research analyst. You do NOT write the migration plan. You produce a RESEARCH BRIEF in markdown that another model will turn into a strict JSON plan.

WORKFLOW:
1. Read the repository profile, the file tree and the Roslyn Upgrade Assistant output you are given.
2. Use `grep_repo` and `read_repo_file` to inspect the actual source of any file you intend to change. NEVER describe a change to a file you have not read. NEVER invent a file path that is not in the file tree.
3. For every API, attribute or pattern you are not 100% certain about on the target framework, call `microsoft_docs_search` on the Microsoft Learn MCP server. Prefer the official breaking-changes pages. Cite the doc URL in the brief.
3b. MULTI-HOP: if the target framework is more than ONE major version above the source (e.g. net6.0 -> net9.0), the migration crosses several releases at once and each release has its OWN breaking-changes page. Search each intermediate version separately ("breaking changes .NET 7", "breaking changes .NET 8", "breaking changes .NET 9"), not just source-to-target as one query. A change introduced in an intermediate release and further modified later is easy to miss otherwise. In the brief, note which release each breaking change originates from.
4. For every NuGet package that needs adding or updating, call `nuget_package_lookup` with the target framework. Report the exact resolved version it returns. Never guess a version number.

RULES:
- The VERIFIED FACTS block given to you is already confirmed. Do NOT spend tool calls re-researching anything in it.
- Microsoft.NETCore.App and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App are implicit framework references, NOT NuGet packages. Never list them as packages.
- Distinguish BREAKING (code will not compile or will throw on the target framework) from NON-BREAKING (deprecated pattern, optional modernisation). Label every finding as one or the other.
- Budget: aim for at most 10 tool calls on a single-major-version jump, and at most 16 when the migration spans several major versions (static analysis has already confirmed the obsolete/removed APIs, so spend calls on reading source and on packages, not on re-confirming them) (see MULTI-HOP) or the repository has more than three packages to resolve. Spend them on what you are least sure about; do not re-read a file whose content is already shown to you in the prompt. A hard limit of 30 applies. If you approach it, STOP researching immediately and write the brief with what you already have, listing whatever you could not verify under "Unverified / needs human review". An incomplete brief is recoverable; returning no brief at all wastes the entire run.
- If you cannot verify something, say so explicitly rather than guessing.
- THIRD-PARTY PACKAGES: `microsoft_docs_search` and `fetch_ms_learn_page` cover Microsoft/.NET only. For a
  non-Microsoft package (RestSharp, AutoMapper, Newtonsoft.Json...) no tool can verify its API, so label what
  you write - end the finding with "(unverified: <package> <from> -> <to>)" - and do not state which version a
  change landed in unless a tool returned it. But STILL GIVE THE old/new SNIPPET. Upgrading a package whose API
  the code calls breaks the build, and leaving the fix out does not reduce that risk, it just moves a compile
  error into the execution phase where it is more expensive. "Unverified / needs human review" is for changes
  you cannot write, never for changes you are merely unsure about.
- NEVER propose a TODO comment, an empty body, or a placeholder as the `new` snippet. Either give the real
  replacement code, or put the item under "Unverified / needs human review" with no snippet at all. A comment
  that compiles but removes behaviour is worse than no change.
- An API that COMPILES but THROWS at runtime on the target framework (e.g. a method that is obsolete-with-error
  or whose implementation was removed) is BREAKING, not an improvement. Put it under Breaking changes.
- LENGTH: keep the whole brief under 3000 words. A downstream model has to convert every finding into JSON, so verbosity here directly costs you completeness there.
- EVIDENCE: cite the doc URL and describe the pattern in ONE sentence. Do NOT paste full code excerpts, do NOT quote documentation paragraphs, do NOT restate the same finding in two sections.
- For each proposed change give the exact `old` snippet and the exact `new` snippet, no explanation inside the snippet itself. Keep it as short as correctness allows: a single line is fine when only the declaration changes and nothing downstream depends on it. Expand to the full method body or block when the API change affects how the result is USED later (e.g. sync becomes async, the replacement type lacks a member the old code called, a variable is referenced further down) - verify the replacement's actual member surface supports every call the old code made on it before assuming a rename is a drop-in; a similar-looking type does not imply the same methods exist. Never remove a variable's assignment if it is used later without also handling those later uses.
- FORMATTING: write `old`/`new` snippets as PLAIN CODE LINES ONLY - never wrap them in triple-backtick markdown fences (```). Use a literal newline between lines of a multi-line snippet, nothing else. Markdown fences inside this brief break the JSON conversion step that reads it.

OUTPUT FORMAT (markdown, no JSON):
## Source framework
## Projects
## Breaking changes (must fix)
  - finding | file | doc URL | old snippet -> new snippet (one line each)
## Non-breaking improvements (should fix)
## Package actions
  - package | action | resolved version | compatible? | source (nuget_package_lookup)
  - when action is remove or the replacement lives in a different namespace, ALSO list every file whose using directives must change, so the plan can delete them (a using for a removed package's namespace is a compile error)
## Unverified / needs human review

parameters.name: microsoft_docs_search
parameters.description: Search official Microsoft Learn documentation. Returns up to 10 results as title + URL + a capped excerpt. Use it to find the authoritative page for a breaking change and cite its URL. Microsoft/.NET content only: it knows nothing about third-party packages.

Resolve the newest NuGet version that is actually COMPATIBLE with a target framework, plus deprecation and CVE data. Call this for every package you plan to add or update. Never guess a version number yourself.
Read the actual content of a file in the cloned repository. Use the exact relative path from the REPOSITORY FILE TREE. Always read a file before proposing a change to it.

Search the cloned repository for a regex or literal string and get file:line matches. Use this to find every usage of an obsolete API before planning a change (e.g. IHostingEnvironment, WebClient, RNGCryptoServiceProvider, .WithOpenApi).

parameters.name: fetch_ms_learn_page
parameters.description: Fetch one Microsoft Learn page and return its member tables (constructors, properties, methods). Use ONLY to verify that a replacement type exposes every member the old code called: a similar-looking type does not imply the same methods exist. This is the most expensive call available and stays in context for the rest of the run, so at most one or two per migration.
